input.document:
# venona ontology -- AI-industry intelligence instance.
#
# What the pipeline may assert about the artificial-intelligence beat: which
# labs, chips, and regulators exist, which models and products they ship, and
# which claims a research/score/graph/brief run may write about them. Same
# contract role as any venona ontology -- schema enums, the extraction guide,
# the writer's predicate whitelist, and the projector's filter are GENERATED
# from this file, not hand-kept in sync with it.
#
# This is a from-scratch design for this domain, not a port. The domain that
# taught the file SHAPE (org-family splits, confusable_with as a real
# boundary, domain/range as an enforced contract) covers prime contractors and
# combatant commands; nothing in its predicate list survives contact with a
# beat where the thing competing for a headline is as often a model or a chip
# as it is a company. Composition, adoption and evaluation are the daily
# claims here, so BUILDS_ON, IMPLEMENTS, ADOPTS and EVALUATED_ON exist and
# FIELDS/COMPONENT_OF do not.

version: 1

# ── the artifact family ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Three artifact types, not one. A single "Product" type was tried first and
# failed on the first archetype checked: "DPO simplifies PPO" and "ChatGPT is
# built on GPT-5.6" and "Claude implements Constitutional AI" are three
# different KINDS of building-on, and a reader asking "what does this model
# depend on" needs the method separated from the artifact separated from the
# thing that measures it. Model, Product and Technique are that split.

entity_types:
  Company:
    color_slot: 1
    prefix: company
    description: >-
      A commercial firm: a for-profit AI lab, a chipmaker or foundry, a
      hyperscaler cloud, an AI-native startup, an enterprise buyer, or an
      investor funding any of those.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that sells AI capability or the hardware under it, or funds
      either. A renamed or restructured division is its own Company linked
      with PART_OF -- "Meta Superintelligence Labs" is a Company, PART_OF
      "Meta Platforms", not a property of it. Sovereign wealth vehicles (MGX,
      PIF, Mubadala) default to Company with org_type investor; move one to
      GovernmentBody only when the sentence is about the state's regulatory
      role, not its money.
    examples: [OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, Mistral AI, DeepSeek, Hugging Face, SoftBank Group]
    org_types: [lab, chipmaker, hyperscaler, startup, enterprise, investor]
    # Four confusable pairs, none of them decorative:
    # - ResearchOrg: OpenAI's nonprofit/PBC split and DeepSeek's "lab" framing
    #   put a for-profit entity and a research entity in the same sentence.
    # - GovernmentBody: a sovereign wealth fund is simultaneously the state's
    #   money and an ordinary investor line-item.
    # - Model: DeepSeek names the company and its flagship model family
    #   identically; so does Mistral. Nothing in the bare string "DeepSeek"
    #   says which one a sentence means.
    # - Product: this domain's startups routinely ship a product under the
    #   company's own name -- Runway, ElevenLabs, Suno, Perplexity,
    #   Midjourney, Hugging Face all name the product after the firm.
    confusable_with: [ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody, Model, Product]

  ResearchOrg:
    color_slot: 2
    prefix: research
    description: >-
      A body that studies or evaluates rather than sells: a nonprofit
      safety/capability evaluator, an academic institute, or an open-research
      collective.
    guidance: >-
      Non-commercial by construction. METR, Epoch AI, Apollo Research, MIRI,
      CAIS, Allen Institute for AI, EleutherAI, Stanford HAI and Mila belong
      here even when they take grants or run paid evaluations for a lab,
      because that is not a sale. A university lab that has spun out a funded
      startup is a Company for the startup and a ResearchOrg for the lab that
      stayed behind.
    examples: [METR, Epoch AI, Apollo Research, Allen Institute for AI, Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, Mila]
    org_types: [eval_org, academic, think_tank, open_collective]
    # GovernmentBody: a national safety institute (UK AISI) does the same
    # technical evaluation work as METR and reads identically in a headline;
    # what differs is who funds and directs it, not what it publishes.
    # Benchmark: LMArena is named identically for the organization that runs
    # the leaderboard and the Elo ranking it publishes -- see Benchmark.
    confusable_with: [GovernmentBody, Benchmark]

  GovernmentBody:
    color_slot: 3
    prefix: govt
    description: >-
      A state or intergovernmental body: a regulator, a standards or safety
      institute, an enforcement agency, or a multinational coordinating body
      with its own staff and budget.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that approves, restricts, or sets binding or voluntary rules
      for AI development or deployment. Use the current name, not a
      superseded one -- the US body is CAISI, not "the AI Safety Institute";
      the UK body is the AI Security Institute, not "AISI" alone once renamed
      in Feb 2025. The European AI Office and the International AI Safety
      Institute Network both qualify as multinational GovernmentBodies: each
      has a standing secretariat and a work programme, unlike a loose bloc
      name with no staff of its own.
    examples: [European AI Office, UK AI Security Institute, "NIST / CAISI", Cyberspace Administration of China, US Federal Trade Commission, International AI Safety Institute Network]
    org_types: [regulator, standards_institute, safety_institute, legislative, multinational]
    confusable_with: []

  Model:
    color_slot: 4
    prefix: model
    description: >-
      A named AI model or model family: the trained artifact and its version
      lineage, independent of the product it ships inside.
    guidance: >-
      Track the family as the stable entity -- "Claude", "GPT-5.6", "Gemini
      3", "Llama 4", "DeepSeek V4", "Qwen" -- and treat point releases (Sonnet
      5, Flash-Lite, R1) as attributes of that entity rather than new ones,
      unless the article is specifically contrasting two versions against each
      other. This is the domain-specific type generic "Product" cannot carry
      alone: competition, fine-tuning lineage and benchmark scoring are all
      claims made about the MODEL, separately from the app or chip it is
      packaged in.
    examples: [Claude, GPT-5.6, Gemini 3, Grok, Llama 4, DeepSeek V4, Qwen, Mistral Large 3]
    model_types: [frontier_closed, open_weight, reasoning, multimodal]
    # Product: a lab's flagship model and its flagship consumer product are
    # routinely the same brand -- "Gemini" is both the model and the app that
    # replaced Bard, "Grok" is both the model and the xAI chatbot. A shared
    # name across this boundary is one thing filed twice.
    confusable_with: [Product]

  Product:
    color_slot: 5
    prefix: product
    description: >-
      A concrete, shippable thing built on or alongside a model: a consumer
      or enterprise application, a coding agent, an enterprise agent
      platform, an AI accelerator chip, a robot, or a named infrastructure
      megaproject.
    guidance: >-
      If it has a product page, a SKU, a price, or ships hardware, it is a
      Product -- software (ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, Salesforce
      Agentforce), silicon (Nvidia Blackwell, Nvidia Rubin, Google TPU
      Ironwood, AWS Trainium), physical robots (Figure 02, Tesla Optimus), or
      a named joint infrastructure build (Stargate). Chips and robots are
      deliberately NOT split into their own types: both are bought, produced,
      adopted and compared exactly the way software products are, and a
      separate type would buy no new predicate.
    examples: [ChatGPT, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Nvidia Rubin, Figure 02, Amazon Bedrock, Stargate, Midjourney]
    product_types: [assistant, coding_agent, enterprise_platform, chip, robot, creative_tool, infra_project]
    confusable_with: []

  Technique:
    color_slot: 6
    prefix: technique
    description: >-
      A method, architecture, or training approach, independent of who uses
      it or what artifact implements it.
    guidance: >-
      Use for reusable methods, not the artifacts built with them --
      "RLHF", "mixture of experts", "Direct Preference Optimization",
      "chain-of-thought prompting", "test-time compute", "Constitutional AI"
      are Techniques; "o3" is a Model that IMPLEMENTS test-time compute. Empty
      confusable_with is deliberate: a named technique and a named model or
      product are never the same reading of a sentence, which is the entire
      reason composition ("X builds on Y") needs both types to exist
      separately.
    examples: [RLHF, Mixture of Experts, Direct Preference Optimization, chain-of-thought prompting, test-time compute, Constitutional AI]
    confusable_with: []

  Benchmark:
    color_slot: 7
    prefix: benchmark
    description: >-
      A named evaluation instrument, test suite, or leaderboard used to
      compare model or product capability.
    guidance: >-
      The measuring stick, not the thing measured -- "SWE-bench Verified",
      "MMLU", "GPQA", "ARC-AGI", "Chatbot Arena" are Benchmarks. The
      organization running a leaderboard is sometimes named identically to
      the leaderboard itself: "LMArena" is used for both the org and the Elo
      ranking it publishes, which is why this is declared confusable with
      ResearchOrg (on that type's side) rather than left for the model to
      guess at silently.
    examples: [SWE-bench Verified, MMLU, GPQA, ARC-AGI, Chatbot Arena]
    confusable_with: []

  Person:
    color_slot: 8
    prefix: person
    description: A named individual in a professional capacity relevant to the AI industry.
    guidance: >-
      Only extract people whose role matters to the relationship being
      asserted -- a founder, a chief scientist, a policy official -- not a
      quoted bystander. A first name shared with a model ("Claude" the person,
      Claude the model) is NOT a type collision to declare: they are two
      things that happen to share a surface, resolved by context, and forcing
      that pair into confusable_with would merge every person named Claude
      into the model on the first ambiguous mention.
    examples: [Ilya Sutskever, Elon Musk, Demis Hassabis, Dario Amodei, Yoshua Bengio]
    confusable_with: []

  Country:
    color_slot: 9
    prefix: country
    description: >-
      A sovereign state: the top-level actor an organization belongs to, or
      the actor behind export controls and national AI strategy.
    guidance: >-
      States only, and only when the article names one as an actor (export
      controls, a national AI approval regime) or as an organization's home.
      NOT blocs: the EU is a GovernmentBody through the European AI Office,
      which has staff and a budget; the International AI Safety Institute
      Network is a coordinating GovernmentBody in its own right for the same
      reason, so its actions belong to it or to its named member institutes,
      never to a bare "the network" treated as a country-like actor. NOT
      regions ("the Gulf", "the West") or cities.
    examples: [United States, China, United Kingdom, France, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia]
    confusable_with: []

# NOT an entity type: "the EU AI Act", "export controls", "the Preparedness
# Framework". Each is a named policy instrument, not a body with a stable
# canonical surface distinct from the GovernmentBody that issues it -- "the EU
# AI Act" is what the European AI Office enforces, not a separate actor, so
# REGULATES takes the GovernmentBody as subject and the Model/Product/Company
# it constrains as object, with the instrument's name left in evidence text.
# Minting a Regulation type for a handful of named acts would strand the same
# way Contract stranded in the domain that taught this file's shape.

predicates:
  PART_OF:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The subject is a constituent division, subsidiary, or restructured unit of the object.
    guidance: >-
      Child --PART_OF--> parent, always. "Meta Superintelligence Labs" is
      PART_OF "Meta Platforms"; "Google DeepMind" is PART_OF "Alphabet" when
      the parent is named. Never put a Country on either side of this --
      a lab's home state is BASED_IN, not a PART_OF ancestor, and never put a
      Model or Product here either -- a model is not a division of the
      company that trains it, it is what PRODUCES asserts instead.
    example: Meta Superintelligence Labs --PART_OF--> Meta Platforms

  BASED_IN:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Country]
    description: The organization's home country of headquarters or incorporation.
    guidance: >-
      One per organization. If a lab has a named national subsidiary or
      office, assert BASED_IN about the subsidiary and let PART_OF carry it
      to the parent rather than re-homing the parent itself.
    example: Mistral AI --BASED_IN--> France

  WORKS_FOR:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: Employment or standing service affiliation.
    example: Ilya Sutskever --WORKS_FOR--> Safe Superintelligence Inc.

  MANAGES:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The organization holds administrative or operating responsibility for a
      joint infrastructure build, distinct from having built any one part of
      it outright.
    guidance: >-
      Reserved for the infra_project product_type -- a megaproject like
      Stargate has several organizations that each MANAGE a stake in it
      without any one of them being sole PRODUCER of the whole. Do not use
      this for an ordinary product a company simply operates alone; that is
      PRODUCES.
    example: OpenAI --MANAGES--> Stargate

  PRODUCES:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    range: [Model, Product]
    description: The organization builds and ships the model or product.
    guidance: >-
      ResearchOrg is in the domain because open-science labs demonstrably
      ship models -- Allen Institute for AI PRODUCES OLMo -- and ResearchOrg
      already sits in EVALUATES and PARTNERS_WITH, so this is consistency,
      not a widening.
    example: Nvidia --PRODUCES--> Nvidia Rubin

  BUILDS_ON:
    domain: [Model, Product, Technique]
    range: [Model, Product, Technique]
    description: >-
      The subject is a derivative, fine-tune, fork, or technical extension of
      the object.
    guidance: >-
      Covers three shapes the press treats as the same underlying claim: a
      model fine-tuned from another model (Perplexity's R1 1776 BUILDS_ON
      DeepSeek-R1), a technique refined from another technique (GRPO
      BUILDS_ON PPO), and a product forked or rebuilt from another product
      (Devin Desktop BUILDS_ON Windsurf). Also covers a product whose
      architecture literally IS a specific model rather than one of several
      interchangeable backends -- ChatGPT BUILDS_ON GPT-5.6. Where a product
      instead offers a model as one of several swappable options via API, use
      ADOPTS, not this: Amazon Bedrock does not BUILD_ON Claude, it ADOPTS it
      alongside a dozen others.
    example: ChatGPT --BUILDS_ON--> GPT-5.6

  IMPLEMENTS:
    domain: [Model, Product]
    range: [Technique]
    description: The model or product is a concrete implementation of the technique.
    example: Claude --IMPLEMENTS--> Constitutional AI

  ADOPTS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody, ResearchOrg, Product]
    range: [Model, Product]
    description: >-
      The subject has deployed or put into production use the model or
      product, as a customer or integrator rather than as its builder.
    guidance: >-
      Covers both org-adopts-artifact ("BMW deploys Figure 02 on a production
      line") and artifact-hosts-artifact ("Amazon Bedrock offers Claude"),
      which is why Product is in the domain: a hosting platform is an actor
      in this domain's press exactly the way a buyer is. Do not use this for
      the organization that built the thing -- that is PRODUCES, and using
      ADOPTS for a builder-of-record understates the claim.
    example: Amazon Bedrock --ADOPTS--> Claude

  COMPETES_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, Model, Product]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, Model, Product]
    symmetric: true
    description: The two compete for the same customers, users, or capability claim.
    guidance: >-
      Symmetric: store once, do not also assert the reverse. Model-to-model
      ("Claude COMPETES_WITH Gemini 3") and product-to-product
      ("Cursor COMPETES_WITH GitHub Copilot") are as routine in this domain's
      press as company-to-company, which is why artifacts are in both
      domain and range, not just Company.
    example: Nvidia Rubin --COMPETES_WITH--> AMD Instinct MI-series

  FUNDS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    description: The subject provided capital, a grant, or a compute/cash commitment to the object.
    guidance: >-
      Covers VC and sovereign-fund rounds, hyperscaler strategic investments,
      and government grants to nonprofits alike; the distinction between an
      equity round and a grant lives in the evidence text, not in a second
      predicate.
    example: SoftBank Group --FUNDS--> OpenAI

  PARTNERS_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    symmetric: true
    description: A cloud/compute supply deal, distribution deal, or joint technical agreement short of ownership or funding.
    example: Amazon (AWS / Amazon AI) --PARTNERS_WITH--> Anthropic

  REGULATES:
    domain: [GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, Model, Product]
    description: >-
      The government body has legal or policy authority to approve, restrict,
      or oversee the object.
    guidance: >-
      Model is in the range because the EU AI Act's binding obligations and
      China's CAC pre-release approval both attach to a named MODEL, not only
      to the company that trained it -- "the CAC approved DeepSeek V4 for
      release" is a REGULATES claim generic company-level regulation cannot
      carry.
    example: Cyberspace Administration of China --REGULATES--> DeepSeek V4

  MEMBER_OF:
    domain: [GovernmentBody]
    range: [GovernmentBody]
    description: The subject is a formal member of a coordinating or standards body.
    guidance: >-
      For named coalitions with their own secretariat, like the International
      AI Safety Institute Network -- not for informal "aligned with" framing
      between regulators that never joined anything.
    example: UK AI Security Institute --MEMBER_OF--> International AI Safety Institute Network

  LEADS:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The person has named leadership responsibility for the organization.
    example: Elon Musk --LEADS--> xAI

  ACQUIRED:
    domain: [Company]
    range: [Company]
    description: The subject acquired the object.
    guidance: Acquirer --ACQUIRED--> acquired. Getting this backwards inverts the corporate history.
    example: Cognition --ACQUIRED--> Windsurf

  EVALUATED_ON:
    domain: [Model, Product]
    range: [Benchmark]
    description: The model or product was measured against this benchmark or leaderboard.
    example: GPT-5.6 --EVALUATED_ON--> SWE-bench Verified

  EVALUATES:
    domain: [ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Model, Product, Company]
    description: >-
      The organization conducted a capability, safety, or compliance
      evaluation of the subject, distinct from the benchmark score itself.
    guidance: >-
      Use this for who RAN the assessment (METR, Apollo Research, UK AISI);
      use EVALUATED_ON for what the artifact scored on a named instrument.
      The two are usually reported in the same article and both should be
      asserted when both are present.
    example: METR --EVALUATES--> Claude

# Archetypes considered and not separately modeled:
# - "membership" for informal blocs (AUKUS-style arrangements) was checked
#   and dropped for the same reason the exemplar domain dropped it: this
#   beat's press asserts MEMBER_OF about named institute networks with a
#   secretariat, never about a bloc with no staff of its own to be a member
#   of anything.

# ── rewrites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Ill-typed shapes the model reaches for that have exactly one safe legal
# rendering. Applied before the domain/range check; the assertion is stamped
# `method='extraction_rewritten'`. A rewrite may only weaken or invert a
# claim, never strengthen it, and every `when` must be ill-typed today while
# every `then` must be well-typed -- the loader enforces both.

rewrites:
  - when:
      predicate: PART_OF
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Country]
    then: { predicate: BASED_IN }
    note: >-
      "OpenAI is part of the United States" is ordinary English and the wrong
      edge; a national organization is BASED_IN its country, never PART_OF it.
  - when:
      predicate: PART_OF
      subject: [Model, Product]
      object: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    then: { predicate: PRODUCES, swap: true }
    note: >-
      "GPT-5.6 is part of OpenAI" is the same miss as the PART_OF/FIELDS
      inversion this file's shape was built to catch -- a model is not a
      division of the company that trains it. PRODUCES swapped is the exact
      same fact the right way round.
  - when:
      predicate: LEADS
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Person]
    then: { predicate: LEADS, swap: true }
    note: Pure inversion; LEADS' subject is always the Person.
  - when:
      predicate: WORKS_FOR
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Person]
    then: { predicate: WORKS_FOR, swap: true }
    note: Same inversion as LEADS, kept as a separate row because it is a separate predicate.

# Infrastructure edges. Written by the projector, never asserted by the model.
internal_predicates:
  MENTIONS: { from: Article, to: Entity }
  FROM_SOURCE: { from: Article, to: Source }
  FEATURED_IN: { from: Article, to: Brief }

    # the leaderboard and the Elo ranking it publishes -- see Benchmark.
    confusable_with: [GovernmentBody, Benchmark]

  GovernmentBody:
    color_slot: 3
    prefix: govt
    description: >-
      A state or intergovernmental body: a regulator, a standards or safety
      institute, an enforcement agency, or a multinational coordinating body
      with its own staff and budget.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that approves, restricts, or sets binding or voluntary rules
      for AI development or deployment. Use the current name, not a
      superseded one -- the US body is CAISI, not "the AI Safety Institute";
      the UK body is the AI Security Institute, not "AISI" alone once renamed
      in Feb 2025. The European AI Office and the International AI Safety
      Institute Network both qualify as multinational GovernmentBodies: each
      has a standing secretariat and a work programme, unlike a loose bloc
      name with no staff of its own.
    examples: [European AI Office, UK AI Security Institute, "NIST / CAISI", Cyberspace Administration of China, US Federal Trade Commission, International AI Safety Institute Network]
    org_types: [regulator, standards_institute, safety_institute, legislative, multinational]
    confusable_with: []

  Model:
    color_slot: 4
    prefix: model
    description: >-
      A named AI model or model family: the trained artifact and its version
      lineage, independent of the product it ships inside.
    guidance: >-
      Track the family as the stable entity -- "Claude", "GPT-5.6", "Gemini
      3", "Llama 4", "DeepSeek V4", "Qwen" -- and treat point releases (Sonnet
      5, Flash-Lite, R1) as attributes of that entity rather than new ones,
      unless the article is specifically contrasting two versions against each
      other. This is the domain-specific type generic "Product" cannot carry
      alone: competition, fine-tuning lineage and benchmark scoring are all
      claims made about the MODEL, separately from the app or chip it is
      packaged in.
    examples: [Claude, GPT-5.6, Gemini 3, Grok, Llama 4, DeepSeek V4, Qwen, Mistral Large 3]
    model_types: [frontier_closed, open_weight, reasoning, multimodal]
    # Product: a lab's flagship model and its flagship consumer product are
    # routinely the same brand -- "Gemini" is both the model and the app that
    # replaced Bard, "Grok" is both the model and the xAI chatbot. A shared
    # name across this boundary is one thing filed twice.
    confusable_with: [Product]

  Product:
    color_slot: 5
    prefix: product
    description: >-
      A concrete, shippable thing built on or alongside a model: a consumer
      or enterprise application, a coding agent, an enterprise agent
      platform, an AI accelerator chip, a robot, or a named infrastructure
      megaproject.
    guidance: >-
      If it has a product page, a SKU, a price, or ships hardware, it is a
      Product -- software (ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, Salesforce
      Agentforce), silicon (Nvidia Blackwell, Nvidia Rubin, Google TPU
      Ironwood, AWS Trainium), physical robots (Figure 02, Tesla Optimus), or
      a named joint infrastructure build (Stargate). Chips and robots are
      deliberately NOT split into their own types: both are bought, produced,
      adopted and compared exactly the way software products are, and a
      separate type would buy no new predicate.
    examples: [ChatGPT, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Nvidia Rubin, Figure 02, Amazon Bedrock, Stargate, Midjourney]
    product_types: [assistant, coding_agent, enterprise_platform, chip, robot, creative_tool, infra_project]
    confusable_with: []

  Technique:
    color_slot: 6
    prefix: technique
    description: >-
      A method, architecture, or training approach, independent of who uses
      it or what artifact implements it.
    guidance: >-
      Use for reusable methods, not the artifacts built with them --
      "RLHF", "mixture of experts", "Direct Preference Optimization",
      "chain-of-thought prompting", "test-time compute", "Constitutional AI"
      are Techniques; "o3" is a Model that IMPLEMENTS test-time compute. Empty
      confusable_with is deliberate: a named technique and a named model or
      product are never the same reading of a sentence, which is the entire
      reason composition ("X builds on Y") needs both types to exist
      separately.
    examples: [RLHF, Mixture of Experts, Direct Preference Optimization, chain-of-thought prompting, test-time compute, Constitutional AI]
    confusable_with: []

  Benchmark:
    color_slot: 7
    prefix: benchmark
    description: >-
      A named evaluation instrument, test suite, or leaderboard used to
      compare model or product capability.
    guidance: >-
      The measuring stick, not the thing measured -- "SWE-bench Verified",
      "MMLU", "GPQA", "ARC-AGI", "Chatbot Arena" are Benchmarks. The
      organization running a leaderboard is sometimes named identically to
      the leaderboard itself: "LMArena" is used for both the org and the Elo
      ranking it publishes, which is why this is declared confusable with
      ResearchOrg (on that type's side) rather than left for the model to
      guess at silently.
    examples: [SWE-bench Verified, MMLU, GPQA, ARC-AGI, Chatbot Arena]
    confusable_with: []

  Person:
    color_slot: 8
    prefix: person
    description: A named individual in a professional capacity relevant to the AI industry.
    guidance: >-
      Only extract people whose role matters to the relationship being
      asserted -- a founder, a chief scientist, a policy official -- not a
      quoted bystander. A first name shared with a model ("Claude" the person,
      Claude the model) is NOT a type collision to declare: they are two
      things that happen to share a surface, resolved by context, and forcing
      that pair into confusable_with would merge every person named Claude
      into the model on the first ambiguous mention.
    examples: [Ilya Sutskever, Elon Musk, Demis Hassabis, Dario Amodei, Yoshua Bengio]
    confusable_with: []

  Country:
    color_slot: 9
    prefix: country
    description: >-
      A sovereign state: the top-level actor an organization belongs to, or
      the actor behind export controls and national AI strategy.
    guidance: >-
      States only, and only when the article names one as an actor (export
      controls, a national AI approval regime) or as an organization's home.
      NOT blocs: the EU is a GovernmentBody through the European AI Office,
      which has staff and a budget; the International AI Safety Institute
      Network is a coordinating GovernmentBody in its own right for the same
      reason, so its actions belong to it or to its named member institutes,
      never to a bare "the network" treated as a country-like actor. NOT
      regions ("the Gulf", "the West") or cities.
    examples: [United States, China, United Kingdom, France, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia]
    confusable_with: []

# NOT an entity type: "the EU AI Act", "export controls", "the Preparedness
# Framework". Each is a named policy instrument, not a body with a stable
# canonical surface distinct from the GovernmentBody that issues it -- "the EU
# AI Act" is what the European AI Office enforces, not a separate actor, so
# REGULATES takes the GovernmentBody as subject and the Model/Product/Company
# it constrains as object, with the instrument's name left in evidence text.
# Minting a Regulation type for a handful of named acts would strand the same
# way Contract stranded in the domain that taught this file's shape.

predicates:
  PART_OF:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The subject is a constituent division, subsidiary, or restructured unit of the object.
    guidance: >-
      Child --PART_OF--> parent, always. "Meta Superintelligence Labs" is
      PART_OF "Meta Platforms"; "Google DeepMind" is PART_OF "Alphabet" when
      the parent is named. Never put a Country on either side of this --
      a lab's home state is BASED_IN, not a PART_OF ancestor, and never put a
      Model or Product here either -- a model is not a division of the
      company that trains it, it is what PRODUCES asserts instead.
    example: Meta Superintelligence Labs --PART_OF--> Meta Platforms

  BASED_IN:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Country]
    description: The organization's home country of headquarters or incorporation.
    guidance: >-
      One per organization. If a lab has a named national subsidiary or
      office, assert BASED_IN about the subsidiary and let PART_OF carry it
      to the parent rather than re-homing the parent itself.
    example: Mistral AI --BASED_IN--> France

  WORKS_FOR:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: Employment or standing service affiliation.
    example: Ilya Sutskever --WORKS_FOR--> Safe Superintelligence Inc.

  MANAGES:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The organization holds administrative or operating responsibility for a
      joint infrastructure build, distinct from having built any one part of
      it outright.
    guidance: >-
      Reserved for the infra_project product_type -- a megaproject like
      Stargate has several organizations that each MANAGE a stake in it
      without any one of them being sole PRODUCER of the whole. Do not use
      this for an ordinary product a company simply operates alone; that is
      PRODUCES.
    example: OpenAI --MANAGES--> Stargate

  PRODUCES:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    range: [Model, Product]
    description: The organization builds and ships the model or product.
    guidance: >-
      ResearchOrg is in the domain because open-science labs demonstrably
      ship models -- Allen Institute for AI PRODUCES OLMo -- and ResearchOrg
      already sits in EVALUATES and PARTNERS_WITH, so this is consistency,
      not a widening.
    example: Nvidia --PRODUCES--> Nvidia Rubin

  BUILDS_ON:
    domain: [Model, Product, Technique]
    range: [Model, Product, Technique]
    description: >-
      The subject is a derivative, fine-tune, fork, or technical extension of
      the object.
    guidance: >-
      Covers three shapes the press treats as the same underlying claim: a
      model fine-tuned from another model (Perplexity's R1 1776 BUILDS_ON
      DeepSeek-R1), a technique refined from another technique (GRPO
      BUILDS_ON PPO), and a product forked or rebuilt from another product
      (Devin Desktop BUILDS_ON Windsurf). Also covers a product whose
      architecture literally IS a specific model rather than one of several
      interchangeable backends -- ChatGPT BUILDS_ON GPT-5.6. Where a product
      instead offers a model as one of several swappable options via API, use
      ADOPTS, not this: Amazon Bedrock does not BUILD_ON Claude, it ADOPTS it
      alongside a dozen others.
    example: ChatGPT --BUILDS_ON--> GPT-5.6

  IMPLEMENTS:
    domain: [Model, Product]
    range: [Technique]
    description: The model or product is a concrete implementation of the technique.
    example: Claude --IMPLEMENTS--> Constitutional AI

  ADOPTS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody, ResearchOrg, Product]
    range: [Model, Product]
    description: >-
      The subject has deployed or put into production use the model or
      product, as a customer or integrator rather than as its builder.
    guidance: >-
      Covers both org-adopts-artifact ("BMW deploys Figure 02 on a production
      line") and artifact-hosts-artifact ("Amazon Bedrock offers Claude"),
      which is why Product is in the domain: a hosting platform is an actor
      in this domain's press exactly the way a buyer is. Do not use this for
      the organization that built the thing -- that is PRODUCES, and using
      ADOPTS for a builder-of-record understates the claim.
    example: Amazon Bedrock --ADOPTS--> Claude

  COMPETES_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, Model, Product]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, Model, Product]
    symmetric: true
    description: The two compete for the same customers, users, or capability claim.
    guidance: >-
      Symmetric: store once, do not also assert the reverse. Model-to-model
      ("Claude COMPETES_WITH Gemini 3") and product-to-product
      ("Cursor COMPETES_WITH GitHub Copilot") are as routine in this domain's
      press as company-to-company, which is why artifacts are in both
      domain and range, not just Company.
    example: Nvidia Rubin --COMPETES_WITH--> AMD Instinct MI-series

  FUNDS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    description: The subject provided capital, a grant, or a compute/cash commitment to the object.
    guidance: >-
      Covers VC and sovereign-fund rounds, hyperscaler strategic investments,
      and government grants to nonprofits alike; the distinction between an
      equity round and a grant lives in the evidence text, not in a second
      predicate.
    example: SoftBank Group --FUNDS--> OpenAI

  PARTNERS_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    symmetric: true
    description: A cloud/compute supply deal, distribution deal, or joint technical agreement short of ownership or funding.
    example: Amazon (AWS / Amazon AI) --PARTNERS_WITH--> Anthropic

  REGULATES:
    domain: [GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, Model, Product]
    description: >-
      The government body has legal or policy authority to approve, restrict,
      or oversee the object.
    guidance: >-
      Model is in the range because the EU AI Act's binding obligations and
      China's CAC pre-release approval both attach to a named MODEL, not only
      to the company that trained it -- "the CAC approved DeepSeek V4 for
      release" is a REGULATES claim generic company-level regulation cannot
      carry.
    example: Cyberspace Administration of China --REGULATES--> DeepSeek V4

  MEMBER_OF:
    domain: [GovernmentBody]
    range: [GovernmentBody]
    description: The subject is a formal member of a coordinating or standards body.
    guidance: >-
      For named coalitions with their own secretariat, like the International
      AI Safety Institute Network -- not for informal "aligned with" framing
      between regulators that never joined anything.
    example: UK AI Security Institute --MEMBER_OF--> International AI Safety Institute Network

  LEADS:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The person has named leadership responsibility for the organization.
    example: Elon Musk --LEADS--> xAI

  ACQUIRED:
    domain: [Company]
    range: [Company]
    description: The subject acquired the object.
    guidance: Acquirer --ACQUIRED--> acquired. Getting this backwards inverts the corporate history.
    example: Cognition --ACQUIRED--> Windsurf

  EVALUATED_ON:
    domain: [Model, Product]
    range: [Benchmark]
    description: The model or product was measured against this benchmark or leaderboard.
    example: GPT-5.6 --EVALUATED_ON--> SWE-bench Verified

  EVALUATES:
    domain: [ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Model, Product, Company]
    description: >-
      The organization conducted a capability, safety, or compliance
      evaluation of the subject, distinct from the benchmark score itself.
    guidance: >-
      Use this for who RAN the assessment (METR, Apollo Research, UK AISI);
      use EVALUATED_ON for what the artifact scored on a named instrument.
      The two are usually reported in the same article and both should be
      asserted when both are present.
    example: METR --EVALUATES--> Claude

# Archetypes considered and not separately modeled:
# - "membership" for informal blocs (AUKUS-style arrangements) was checked
#   and dropped for the same reason the exemplar domain dropped it: this
#   beat's press asserts MEMBER_OF about named institute networks with a
#   secretariat, never about a bloc with no staff of its own to be a member
#   of anything.

# ── rewrites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Ill-typed shapes the model reaches for that have exactly one safe legal
# rendering. Applied before the domain/range check; the assertion is stamped
# `method='extraction_rewritten'`. A rewrite may only weaken or invert a
# claim, never strengthen it, and every `when` must be ill-typed today while
# every `then` must be well-typed -- the loader enforces both.

rewrites:
  - when:
      predicate: PART_OF
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Country]
    then: { predicate: BASED_IN }
    note: >-
      "OpenAI is part of the United States" is ordinary English and the wrong
      edge; a national organization is BASED_IN its country, never PART_OF it.
  - when:
      predicate: PART_OF
      subject: [Model, Product]
      object: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    then: { predicate: PRODUCES, swap: true }
    note: >-
      "GPT-5.6 is part of OpenAI" is the same miss as the PART_OF/FIELDS
      inversion this file's shape was built to catch -- a model is not a
      division of the company that trains it. PRODUCES swapped is the exact
      same fact the right way round.
  - when:
      predicate: LEADS
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Person]
    then: { predicate: LEADS, swap: true }
    note: Pure inversion; LEADS' subject is always the Person.
  - when:
      predicate: WORKS_FOR
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Person]
    then: { predicate: WORKS_FOR, swap: true }
    note: Same inversion as LEADS, kept as a separate row because it is a separate predicate.

# Infrastructure edges. Written by the projector, never asserted by the model.
internal_predicates:
  MENTIONS: { from: Article, to: Entity }
  FROM_SOURCE: { from: Article, to: Source }
  FEATURED_IN: { from: Article, to: Brief }

structured_output.document:
# venona ontology -- AI-industry intelligence instance.
#
# What the pipeline may assert about the artificial-intelligence beat: which
# labs, chips, and regulators exist, which models and products they ship, and
# which claims a research/score/graph/brief run may write about them. Same
# contract role as any venona ontology -- schema enums, the extraction guide,
# the writer's predicate whitelist, and the projector's filter are GENERATED
# from this file, not hand-kept in sync with it.
#
# This is a from-scratch design for this domain, not a port. The domain that
# taught the file SHAPE (org-family splits, confusable_with as a real
# boundary, domain/range as an enforced contract) covers prime contractors and
# combatant commands; nothing in its predicate list survives contact with a
# beat where the thing competing for a headline is as often a model or a chip
# as it is a company. Composition, adoption and evaluation are the daily
# claims here, so BUILDS_ON, IMPLEMENTS, ADOPTS and EVALUATED_ON exist and
# FIELDS/COMPONENT_OF do not.

version: 1

# ── the artifact family ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Three artifact types, not one. A single "Product" type was tried first and
# failed on the first archetype checked: "DPO simplifies PPO" and "ChatGPT is
# built on GPT-5.6" and "Claude implements Constitutional AI" are three
# different KINDS of building-on, and a reader asking "what does this model
# depend on" needs the method separated from the artifact separated from the
# thing that measures it. Model, Product and Technique are that split.

entity_types:
  Company:
    color_slot: 1
    prefix: company
    description: >-
      A commercial firm: a for-profit AI lab, a chipmaker or foundry, a
      hyperscaler cloud, an AI-native startup, an enterprise buyer, or an
      investor funding any of those.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that sells AI capability or the hardware under it, or funds
      either. A renamed or restructured division is its own Company linked
      with PART_OF -- "Meta Superintelligence Labs" is a Company, PART_OF
      "Meta Platforms", not a property of it. Sovereign wealth vehicles (MGX,
      PIF, Mubadala) default to Company with org_type investor; move one to
      GovernmentBody only when the sentence is about the state's regulatory
      role, not its money.
    examples: [OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, Mistral AI, DeepSeek, Hugging Face, SoftBank Group]
    org_types: [lab, chipmaker, hyperscaler, startup, enterprise, investor]
    # Four confusable pairs, none of them decorative:
    # - ResearchOrg: OpenAI's nonprofit/PBC split and DeepSeek's "lab" framing
    #   put a for-profit entity and a research entity in the same sentence.
    # - GovernmentBody: a sovereign wealth fund is simultaneously the state's
    #   money and an ordinary investor line-item.
    # - Model: DeepSeek names the company and its flagship model family
    #   identically; so does Mistral. Nothing in the bare string "DeepSeek"
    #   says which one a sentence means.
    # - Product: this domain's startups routinely ship a product under the
    #   company's own name -- Runway, ElevenLabs, Suno, Perplexity,
    #   Midjourney, Hugging Face all name the product after the firm.
    confusable_with: [ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody, Model, Product]

  ResearchOrg:
    color_slot: 2
    prefix: research
    description: >-
      A body that studies or evaluates rather than sells: a nonprofit
      safety/capability evaluator, an academic institute, or an open-research
      collective.
    guidance: >-
      Non-commercial by construction. METR, Epoch AI, Apollo Research, MIRI,
      CAIS, Allen Institute for AI, EleutherAI, Stanford HAI and Mila belong
      here even when they take grants or run paid evaluations for a lab,
      because that is not a sale. A university lab that has spun out a funded
      startup is a Company for the startup and a ResearchOrg for the lab that
      stayed behind.
    examples: [METR, Epoch AI, Apollo Research, Allen Institute for AI, Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, Mila]
    org_types: [eval_org, academic, think_tank, open_collective]
    # GovernmentBody: a national safety institute (UK AISI) does the same
    # technical evaluation work as METR and reads identically in a headline;
    # what differs is who funds and directs it, not what it publishes.
    # Benchmark: LMArena is named identically for the organization that runs
    # the leaderboard and the Elo ranking it publishes -- see Benchmark.
    confusable_with: [GovernmentBody, Benchmark]

  GovernmentBody:
    color_slot: 3
    prefix: govt
    description: >-
      A state or intergovernmental body: a regulator, a standards or safety
      institute, an enforcement agency, or a multinational coordinating body
      with its own staff and budget.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that approves, restricts, or sets binding or voluntary rules
      for AI development or deployment. Use the current name, not a
      superseded one -- the US body is CAISI, not "the AI Safety Institute";
      the UK body is the AI Security Institute, not "AISI" alone once renamed
      in Feb 2025. The European AI Office and the International AI Safety
      Institute Network both qualify as multinational GovernmentBodies: each
      has a standing secretariat and a work programme, unlike a loose bloc
      name with no staff of its own.
    examples: [European AI Office, UK AI Security Institute, "NIST / CAISI", Cyberspace Administration of China, US Federal Trade Commission, International AI Safety Institute Network]
    org_types: [regulator, standards_institute, safety_institute, legislative, multinational]
    confusable_with: []

  Model:
    color_slot: 4
    prefix: model
    description: >-
      A named AI model or model family: the trained artifact and its version
      lineage, independent of the product it ships inside.
    guidance: >-
      Track the family as the stable entity -- "Claude", "GPT-5.6", "Gemini
      3", "Llama 4", "DeepSeek V4", "Qwen" -- and treat point releases (Sonnet
      5, Flash-Lite, R1) as attributes of that entity rather than new ones,
      unless the article is specifically contrasting two versions against each
      other. This is the domain-specific type generic "Product" cannot carry
      alone: competition, fine-tuning lineage and benchmark scoring are all
      claims made about the MODEL, separately from the app or chip it is
      packaged in.
    examples: [Claude, GPT-5.6, Gemini 3, Grok, Llama 4, DeepSeek V4, Qwen, Mistral Large 3]
    model_types: [frontier_closed, open_weight, reasoning, multimodal]
    # Product: a lab's flagship model and its flagship consumer product are
    # routinely the same brand -- "Gemini" is both the model and the app that
    # replaced Bard, "Grok" is both the model and the xAI chatbot. A shared
    # name across this boundary is one thing filed twice.
    confusable_with: [Product]

  Product:
    color_slot: 5
    prefix: product
    description: >-
      A concrete, shippable thing built on or alongside a model: a consumer
      or enterprise application, a coding agent, an enterprise agent
      platform, an AI accelerator chip, a robot, or a named infrastructure
      megaproject.
    guidance: >-
      If it has a product page, a SKU, a price, or ships hardware, it is a
      Product -- software (ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, Salesforce
      Agentforce), silicon (Nvidia Blackwell, Nvidia Rubin, Google TPU
      Ironwood, AWS Trainium), physical robots (Figure 02, Tesla Optimus), or
      a named joint infrastructure build (Stargate). Chips and robots are
      deliberately NOT split into their own types: both are bought, produced,
      adopted and compared exactly the way software products are, and a
      separate type would buy no new predicate.
    examples: [ChatGPT, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Nvidia Rubin, Figure 02, Amazon Bedrock, Stargate, Midjourney]
    product_types: [assistant, coding_agent, enterprise_platform, chip, robot, creative_tool, infra_project]
    confusable_with: []

  Technique:
    color_slot: 6
    prefix: technique
    description: >-
      A method, architecture, or training approach, independent of who uses
      it or what artifact implements it.
    guidance: >-
      Use for reusable methods, not the artifacts built with them --
      "RLHF", "mixture of experts", "Direct Preference Optimization",
      "chain-of-thought prompting", "test-time compute", "Constitutional AI"
      are Techniques; "o3" is a Model that IMPLEMENTS test-time compute. Empty
      confusable_with is deliberate: a named technique and a named model or
      product are never the same reading of a sentence, which is the entire
      reason composition ("X builds on Y") needs both types to exist
      separately.
    examples: [RLHF, Mixture of Experts, Direct Preference Optimization, chain-of-thought prompting, test-time compute, Constitutional AI]
    confusable_with: []

  Benchmark:
    color_slot: 7
    prefix: benchmark
    description: >-
      A named evaluation instrument, test suite, or leaderboard used to
      compare model or product capability.
    guidance: >-
      The measuring stick, not the thing measured -- "SWE-bench Verified",
      "MMLU", "GPQA", "ARC-AGI", "Chatbot Arena" are Benchmarks. The
      organization running a leaderboard is sometimes named identically to
      the leaderboard itself: "LMArena" is used for both the org and the Elo
      ranking it publishes, which is why this is declared confusable with
      ResearchOrg (on that type's side) rather than left for the model to
      guess at silently.
    examples: [SWE-bench Verified, MMLU, GPQA, ARC-AGI, Chatbot Arena]
    confusable_with: []

  Person:
    color_slot: 8
    prefix: person
    description: A named individual in a professional capacity relevant to the AI industry.
    guidance: >-
      Only extract people whose role matters to the relationship being
      asserted -- a founder, a chief scientist, a policy official -- not a
      quoted bystander. A first name shared with a model ("Claude" the person,
      Claude the model) is NOT a type collision to declare: they are two
      things that happen to share a surface, resolved by context, and forcing
      that pair into confusable_with would merge every person named Claude
      into the model on the first ambiguous mention.
    examples: [Ilya Sutskever, Elon Musk, Demis Hassabis, Dario Amodei, Yoshua Bengio]
    confusable_with: []

  Country:
    color_slot: 9
    prefix: country
    description: >-
      A sovereign state: the top-level actor an organization belongs to, or
      the actor behind export controls and national AI strategy.
    guidance: >-
      States only, and only when the article names one as an actor (export
      controls, a national AI approval regime) or as an organization's home.
      NOT blocs: the EU is a GovernmentBody through the European AI Office,
      which has staff and a budget; the International AI Safety Institute
      Network is a coordinating GovernmentBody in its own right for the same
      reason, so its actions belong to it or to its named member institutes,
      never to a bare "the network" treated as a country-like actor. NOT
      regions ("the Gulf", "the West") or cities.
    examples: [United States, China, United Kingdom, France, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia]
    confusable_with: []

# NOT an entity type: "the EU AI Act", "export controls", "the Preparedness
# Framework". Each is a named policy instrument, not a body with a stable
# canonical surface distinct from the GovernmentBody that issues it -- "the EU
# AI Act" is what the European AI Office enforces, not a separate actor, so
# REGULATES takes the GovernmentBody as subject and the Model/Product/Company
# it constrains as object, with the instrument's name left in evidence text.
# Minting a Regulation type for a handful of named acts would strand the same
# way Contract stranded in the domain that taught this file's shape.

predicates:
  PART_OF:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The subject is a constituent division, subsidiary, or restructured unit of the object.
    guidance: >-
      Child --PART_OF--> parent, always. "Meta Superintelligence Labs" is
      PART_OF "Meta Platforms"; "Google DeepMind" is PART_OF "Alphabet" when
      the parent is named. Never put a Country on either side of this --
      a lab's home state is BASED_IN, not a PART_OF ancestor, and never put a
      Model or Product here either -- a model is not a division of the
      company that trains it, it is what PRODUCES asserts instead.
    example: Meta Superintelligence Labs --PART_OF--> Meta Platforms

  BASED_IN:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Country]
    description: The organization's home country of headquarters or incorporation.
    guidance: >-
      One per organization. If a lab has a named national subsidiary or
      office, assert BASED_IN about the subsidiary and let PART_OF carry it
      to the parent rather than re-homing the parent itself.
    example: Mistral AI --BASED_IN--> France

  WORKS_FOR:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: Employment or standing service affiliation.
    example: Ilya Sutskever --WORKS_FOR--> Safe Superintelligence Inc.

  MANAGES:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The organization holds administrative or operating responsibility for a
      joint infrastructure build, distinct from having built any one part of
      it outright.
    guidance: >-
      Reserved for the infra_project product_type -- a megaproject like
      Stargate has several organizations that each MANAGE a stake in it
      without any one of them being sole PRODUCER of the whole. Do not use
      this for an ordinary product a company simply operates alone; that is
      PRODUCES.
    example: OpenAI --MANAGES--> Stargate

  PRODUCES:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    range: [Model, Product]
    description: The organization builds and ships the model or product.
    guidance: >-
      ResearchOrg is in the domain because open-science labs demonstrably
      ship models -- Allen Institute for AI PRODUCES OLMo -- and ResearchOrg
      already sits in EVALUATES and PARTNERS_WITH, so this is consistency,
      not a widening.
    example: Nvidia --PRODUCES--> Nvidia Rubin

  BUILDS_ON:
    domain: [Model, Product, Technique]
    range: [Model, Product, Technique]
    description: >-
      The subject is a derivative, fine-tune, fork, or technical extension of
      the object.
    guidance: >-
      Covers three shapes the press treats as the same underlying claim: a
      model fine-tuned from another model (Perplexity's R1 1776 BUILDS_ON
      DeepSeek-R1), a technique refined from another technique (GRPO
      BUILDS_ON PPO), and a product forked or rebuilt from another product
      (Devin Desktop BUILDS_ON Windsurf). Also covers a product whose
      architecture literally IS a specific model rather than one of several
      interchangeable backends -- ChatGPT BUILDS_ON GPT-5.6. Where a product
      instead offers a model as one of several swappable options via API, use
      ADOPTS, not this: Amazon Bedrock does not BUILD_ON Claude, it ADOPTS it
      alongside a dozen others.
    example: ChatGPT --BUILDS_ON--> GPT-5.6

  IMPLEMENTS:
    domain: [Model, Product]
    range: [Technique]
    description: The model or product is a concrete implementation of the technique.
    example: Claude --IMPLEMENTS--> Constitutional AI

  ADOPTS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody, ResearchOrg, Product]
    range: [Model, Product]
    description: >-
      The subject has deployed or put into production use the model or
      product, as a customer or integrator rather than as its builder.
    guidance: >-
      Covers both org-adopts-artifact ("BMW deploys Figure 02 on a production
      line") and artifact-hosts-artifact ("Amazon Bedrock offers Claude"),
      which is why Product is in the domain: a hosting platform is an actor
      in this domain's press exactly the way a buyer is. Do not use this for
      the organization that built the thing -- that is PRODUCES, and using
      ADOPTS for a builder-of-record understates the claim.
    example: Amazon Bedrock --ADOPTS--> Claude

  COMPETES_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, Model, Product]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, Model, Product]
    symmetric: true
    description: The two compete for the same customers, users, or capability claim.
    guidance: >-
      Symmetric: store once, do not also assert the reverse. Model-to-model
      ("Claude COMPETES_WITH Gemini 3") and product-to-product
      ("Cursor COMPETES_WITH GitHub Copilot") are as routine in this domain's
      press as company-to-company, which is why artifacts are in both
      domain and range, not just Company.
    example: Nvidia Rubin --COMPETES_WITH--> AMD Instinct MI-series

  FUNDS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    description: The subject provided capital, a grant, or a compute/cash commitment to the object.
    guidance: >-
      Covers VC and sovereign-fund rounds, hyperscaler strategic investments,
      and government grants to nonprofits alike; the distinction between an
      equity round and a grant lives in the evidence text, not in a second
      predicate.
    example: SoftBank Group --FUNDS--> OpenAI

  PARTNERS_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    symmetric: true
    description: A cloud/compute supply deal, distribution deal, or joint technical agreement short of ownership or funding.
    example: Amazon (AWS / Amazon AI) --PARTNERS_WITH--> Anthropic

  REGULATES:
    domain: [GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, Model, Product]
    description: >-
      The government body has legal or policy authority to approve, restrict,
      or oversee the object.
    guidance: >-
      Model is in the range because the EU AI Act's binding obligations and
      China's CAC pre-release approval both attach to a named MODEL, not only
      to the company that trained it -- "the CAC approved DeepSeek V4 for
      release" is a REGULATES claim generic company-level regulation cannot
      carry.
    example: Cyberspace Administration of China --REGULATES--> DeepSeek V4

  MEMBER_OF:
    domain: [GovernmentBody]
    range: [GovernmentBody]
    description: The subject is a formal member of a coordinating or standards body.
    guidance: >-
      For named coalitions with their own secretariat, like the International
      AI Safety Institute Network -- not for informal "aligned with" framing
      between regulators that never joined anything.
    example: UK AI Security Institute --MEMBER_OF--> International AI Safety Institute Network

  LEADS:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The person has named leadership responsibility for the organization.
    example: Elon Musk --LEADS--> xAI

  ACQUIRED:
    domain: [Company]
    range: [Company]
    description: The subject acquired the object.
    guidance: Acquirer --ACQUIRED--> acquired. Getting this backwards inverts the corporate history.
    example: Cognition --ACQUIRED--> Windsurf

  EVALUATED_ON:
    domain: [Model, Product]
    range: [Benchmark]
    description: The model or product was measured against this benchmark or leaderboard.
    example: GPT-5.6 --EVALUATED_ON--> SWE-bench Verified

  EVALUATES:
    domain: [ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Model, Product, Company]
    description: >-
      The organization conducted a capability, safety, or compliance
      evaluation of the subject, distinct from the benchmark score itself.
    guidance: >-
      Use this for who RAN the assessment (METR, Apollo Research, UK AISI);
      use EVALUATED_ON for what the artifact scored on a named instrument.
      The two are usually reported in the same article and both should be
      asserted when both are present.
    example: METR --EVALUATES--> Claude

# Archetypes considered and not separately modeled:
# - "membership" for informal blocs (AUKUS-style arrangements) was checked
#   and dropped for the same reason the exemplar domain dropped it: this
#   beat's press asserts MEMBER_OF about named institute networks with a
#   secretariat, never about a bloc with no staff of its own to be a member
#   of anything.

# ── rewrites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Ill-typed shapes the model reaches for that have exactly one safe legal
# rendering. Applied before the domain/range check; the assertion is stamped
# `method='extraction_rewritten'`. A rewrite may only weaken or invert a
# claim, never strengthen it, and every `when` must be ill-typed today while
# every `then` must be well-typed -- the loader enforces both.

rewrites:
  - when:
      predicate: PART_OF
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Country]
    then: { predicate: BASED_IN }
    note: >-
      "OpenAI is part of the United States" is ordinary English and the wrong
      edge; a national organization is BASED_IN its country, never PART_OF it.
  - when:
      predicate: PART_OF
      subject: [Model, Product]
      object: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    then: { predicate: PRODUCES, swap: true }
    note: >-
      "GPT-5.6 is part of OpenAI" is the same miss as the PART_OF/FIELDS
      inversion this file's shape was built to catch -- a model is not a
      division of the company that trains it. PRODUCES swapped is the exact
      same fact the right way round.
  - when:
      predicate: LEADS
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Person]
    then: { predicate: LEADS, swap: true }
    note: Pure inversion; LEADS' subject is always the Person.
  - when:
      predicate: WORKS_FOR
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Person]
    then: { predicate: WORKS_FOR, swap: true }
    note: Same inversion as LEADS, kept as a separate row because it is a separate predicate.

# Infrastructure edges. Written by the projector, never asserted by the model.
internal_predicates:
  MENTIONS: { from: Article, to: Entity }
  FROM_SOURCE: { from: Article, to: Source }
  FEATURED_IN: { from: Article, to: Brief }

changelog:
  - version: 1
    date: "2026-08-31"
    change: Initial generated ontology for the AI-industry intelligence domain.
